title: Find an opposite side from the sine ratio in a 3-5 family
source: Theory IGCSE-15.3 Quick check 1 (sin A=3/5, hyp=20, opp=12); book sine-ratio work on printed pp.489–490, new numbers
stem: In a right-angled triangle, \(\sin A=3/5\) and the hypotenuse is {H|int} cm. What is the length, in centimetres, of the opposite side to \(A\)?

steps.name: A
steps.note: O is 3k and H is 5k. Original k=4 gives hyp 20 and opp 12.

title: Find an opposite side using tan of 45 degrees
source: Theory IGCSE-15.3 Quick check 2 (adj=9, angle 45, opp=9); book tan-ratio work on printed p.481, new numbers
stem: In a right-angled triangle the adjacent side to a \(45^\circ\) angle is {a|int} cm. What is the length, in centimetres, of the opposite side?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \(\tan 45^\circ=1\), so the opposite side equals the adjacent side and is {O|int} cm.

title: Find an adjacent side from the cosine ratio 1/2
source: Theory IGCSE-15.3 Quick check 3 (cos A=1/2, hyp=10, adj=5); book cosine-ratio work on printed pp.489–490, new numbers
stem: In a right-angled triangle, \(\cos A=1/2\) and the hypotenuse is {H|int} cm. What is the length, in centimetres, of the adjacent side to \(A\)?

steps.name: A
steps.note: ADJ is k/2 and H is k. Original: 10/2=5.

title: Height of a post from an angle of elevation of 19 degrees

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2019), Question 4(a) only, including the length BC=107 m which is labelled on the official diagram. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Parts 4(b) to 4(e) are omitted (cosine rule, sine rule, area, and a bearing).

stem:
This question is 0580/43/O/N/19 Question 4(a), taken from the official QP.

The diagram shows a field, \(ABCD\), on horizontal ground, with \(BC=107\) m.

(a) There is a vertical post at \(C\).
From \(B\), the angle of elevation of the top of the post is \(19^\circ\).

Find the height of the post.  [2]

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: The horizontal distance from \(B\) to the post is 107 m, so if \(h\) is the height of the post then \(h/107=\tan 19^\circ\), or equivalently \(h/\sin 19^\circ=107/\sin 71^\circ\).
steps.note: MS 4(a): M1 for h/107=tan 19 or h/sin 19 = 107/sin 71, or better. Independent: h=107 tan 19.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \(h=107\tan 19^\circ=36.843\ldots\), so the height is 36.8 m, to 3 significant figures.
steps.note: MS 4(a): 36.8 or 36.84 to 36.84... for 2 marks. Independent: 107 tan 19 degrees = 36.84305... = 36.8 to 3 s.f.
